claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct Malaysian Malay term for wife; PRPM defines it as a woman who is a life partner or a married woman.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer “isteri”

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Wife” matches the sense “a married woman in relation to her spouse.”
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: “Different-common-word” is acceptable because Indonesian standard spelling is “istri” while Malaysian standard spelling is “isteri,” despite their shared meaning and origin.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation

claim_reviews.conclusion: No contrast is required; “istri” and “isteri” are not false friends.
claim_reviews.evidence_limitation: No dedicated false-friend source was necessary because both dictionary definitions directly establish the shared sense.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both forms are correct standard national variants for “wife,” the English cue and sense align, and the different-common-word relation is acceptable for learner-facing contrast. No false-friend contrast is needed because the forms share the same meaning.
